Mereka memberikan hadiah dan pemberian yang besar kepada para peminta, dan menguasai desa-desa dan perkebunan di pedalaman dan kota-kota di seluruh kerajaan, hingga mereka membuat marah orang-orang dekat (khalifah), menimbulkan dendam pada kalangan khusus, dan membuat tersedak para pemegang jabatan. Maka tersingkaplah bagi mereka wajah-wajah persaingan dan kedengkian, dan kalajengking-kalajengking fitnah merayap ke tempat tidur mereka yang empuk dalam negara. Bahkan Bani Qahthabah, paman-paman Ja'far dari pihak ibu, termasuk orang-orang yang paling gencar memfitnah mereka; ikatan rahim tidak membuat mereka berbelas kasih karena kedengkian yang tertanam dalam jiwa mereka, dan ikatan kekerabatan tidak mencegah mereka. Hal itu bersamaan dengan timbulnya kecemburuan dalam diri tuan mereka (khalifah) dan keengganan terhadap pengekangan dan rasa tinggi hati. Dendam-dendam yang ditimbulkan oleh kesombongan-kesombongan kecil mereka dan sikap mereka yang terus-menerus berujung pada pelanggaran-pelanggaran besar, seperti kisah mereka dengan Yahya bin 'Abdullah bin Hasan bin al-Hasan bin 'Ali bin Abi Thalib, saudara Muhammad al-Mahdi yang dijuluki an-Nafs az-Zakiyyah yang memberontak terhadap al-Manshur. Yahya inilah yang diturunkan oleh al-Fadhl bin Yahya dari negeri Dailam dengan jaminan keamanan dari ar-Rasyid dengan tulisan tangannya, dan ia memberikan kepada mereka (penduduk Dailam) untuknya sejuta dirham, menurut yang disebutkan ath-Thabari. Ar-Rasyid menyerahkannya kepada Ja'far dan menjadikan penahanannya di rumah dan di bawah pengawasannya. Ja'far menahannya beberapa waktu, kemudian keakrabannya (dengan khalifah) mendorongnya untuk melepaskannya dan bertindak sendiri dalam melepaskan ikatannya, karena menurut anggapannya menjaga darah Ahlul Bait, dan karena merasa akrab dengan sultan dalam keputusannya. Ar-Rasyid menanyakan kepadanya tentang Yahya ketika hal itu dilaporkan kepadanya; Ja'far menyadarinya dan berkata: "Aku telah melepaskannya." Ar-Rasyid menampakkan wajah
40.en: his nest under his wing, and Yahya controlled his affairs; Harun used to call him 'father'. As a result, the ruler's favour turned towards them, their familiarity grew, their influence spread, all faces turned to them, all necks bent to them, all hopes were set on them, and gifts of kings and presents of amirs came to them from the remotest borders. The tax revenues found their way into their treasury as a means of seeking their favour and goodwill. They gave lavishly to the men of the Shi'a and to important relatives (of the Prophet), and obliged them with their benefactions; they gave to poor members of noble houses, freed captives, and were praised as their caliph was not. They gave large gifts and presents to those who asked them for something, and gained control of villages and estates in the countryside and cities in all the provinces. Eventually they angered the inner circle, aroused the rancour of the elite and offended the holders of office. Rivalry and envy were revealed to them, and the scorpions of slander crept into their soft beds in the dynasty. The Banu Qahtaba, Ja'far's maternal uncles, were among the most active slanderers; the ties of kinship did not make them relent because of the envy in their hearts, nor did the bonds of relationship restrain them. In their master this coincided with incipient jealousy, dislike of restraint and pride. The resentment caused by their small acts of presumption and their persistence led to great offences, such as their affair with Yahya ibn 'Abdallah ibn Hasan ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, brother of Muhammad al-Mahdi called the Pure Soul, who rebelled against al-Mansur. This Yahya was brought down from Daylam by al-Fadl ibn Yahya under a safe-conduct from ar-Rashid in his own hand, al-Fadl paying the Daylamites a million dirhams for him, according to at-Tabari. Ar-Rashid handed him over to Ja'far and put him under arrest in his house and under his supervision. Ja'far kept him in prison for a time, but then his presumption led him to release him and to undo his bonds on his own authority, out of respect, as he claimed, for the blood of the Prophet's family, and out of presumption on the ruler's judgement. When this was reported to ar-Rashid he asked Ja'far about it; Ja'far realised and said: 'I have released him.' Ar-Rashid outwardly showed

41.id: persetujuan kepadanya, tetapi menyimpannya dalam hatinya. Dengan itu Ja'far membuka jalan (kehancuran) atas dirinya dan kaumnya, hingga singgasana mereka diruntuhkan, langit mereka dijatuhkan atas mereka, bumi menelan mereka dan rumah mereka, dan hari-hari mereka menjadi pendahulu dan perumpamaan bagi orang-orang sesudahnya. Barang siapa merenungkan kabar-kabar mereka dan menelusuri perjalanan negara dan perjalanan hidup mereka, ia akan mendapati hal itu terbukti jejaknya dan tersusun sebab-sebabnya. Lihatlah apa yang dinukil Ibnu 'Abdi Rabbih tentang percakapan ar-Rasyid dengan paman kakeknya, Dawud bin 'Ali, mengenai kehancuran mereka, dan apa yang ia sebutkan dalam bab para penyair dalam kitab al-'Iqd tentang percakapan al-Ashma'i dengan ar-Rasyid dan al-Fadhl bin Yahya dalam obrolan malam mereka; engkau akan memahami bahwa yang membunuh mereka hanyalah kecemburuan dan persaingan dalam memonopoli kekuasaan, dari khalifah hingga orang-orang di bawahnya. Demikian pula tipu daya yang dilakukan musuh-musuh mereka dari kalangan orang dalam, dengan menyisipkan syair kepada para penyanyi sebagai siasat agar didengar oleh khalifah dan membangkitkan amarahnya terhadap mereka, yaitu:
41.en: approval, but he concealed the matter in his heart. Thus Ja'far opened the way to the destruction of himself and his people, until their throne was overthrown, their heaven fell upon them, the earth swallowed them and their house, and their days became an example and a warning to others. Whoever studies their history and investigates the ways of the dynasty and their own ways will find this to be well documented and its causes well established. Look at what Ibn 'Abd Rabbih reports about ar-Rashid's conversation with his great-uncle Dawud ibn 'Ali concerning their destruction, and what he mentions in the chapter on poets in the 'Iqd about al-Asma'i's conversation with ar-Rashid and al-Fadl ibn Yahya in their evening sessions; you will understand that it was only jealousy and rivalry for control, on the part of the caliph and those beneath him, that killed them. So too the stratagem of their enemies among the courtiers, who slipped to the singers verses meant to be heard by the caliph and to stir up his resentment against them:

42.id: Andai Hindun menepati janjinya kepada kami ... dan menyembuhkan jiwa kami dari apa yang kami rasakan,
42.en: Would that Hind had fulfilled her promise to us ... and healed our souls of what we feel,

43.id: dan sekali saja bertindak sendiri (istabaddat) ... sesungguhnya orang yang lemah adalah yang tidak bertindak sendiri.
43.en: and acted on her own just once; ... the weakling is he who never acts on his own.

44.id: Ketika ar-Rasyid mendengarnya, ia berkata: "Ya, demi Allah, aku adalah orang yang lemah." Hingga dengan hal-hal semacam ini mereka membangkitkan kecemburuannya yang terpendam dan menimpakan kepada mereka kerasnya pembalasannya. Kami berlindung kepada Allah dari dikuasai orang lain dan buruknya keadaan.
44.en: When ar-Rashid heard it he said: 'Yes, by Allah, I am a weakling.' By such means they roused his latent jealousy and loosed upon them the force of his vengeance. We seek refuge in Allah from being overpowered by men and from an evil state.

45.id: Adapun apa yang dihiaskan oleh kisah itu tentang ar-Rasyid yang gemar minum khamar dan mabuknya bersamaan dengan mabuknya para teman minum, Mahasuci Allah, kami tidak mengetahui keburukan apa pun padanya. Di mana hal itu dibandingkan keadaan ar-Rasyid dan penegakannya terhadap kewajiban jabatan khilafah berupa agama dan keadilan, serta persahabatannya dengan para ulama dan wali, percakapannya dengan al-Fudhail bin 'Iyadh, Ibnu as-Sammak, dan al-'Umari, surat-menyuratnya dengan Sufyan ats-Tsauri, tangisannya karena nasihat-nasihat mereka, doanya di Makkah dalam thawafnya, ibadahnya, penjagaannya terhadap waktu-waktu shalat, dan kehadirannya pada shalat Subuh di awal waktunya? Ath-Thabari dan lainnya menceritakan bahwa ia shalat seratus rakaat sunnah setiap hari, berperang satu tahun dan berhaji satu tahun. Ia pernah menghardik Ibnu Abi Maryam, pelawaknya dalam obrolan malam, ketika ia melontarkan lelucon semacam itu dalam shalat; ketika ia mendengar ar-Rasyid membaca: "Dan mengapa aku tidak menyembah (Allah) yang telah menciptakanku" (QS. Yasin: 22), ia berkata: "Demi Allah, aku tidak tahu mengapa!" Ar-Rasyid tidak dapat menahan tawa, kemudian menoleh kepadanya dengan marah dan berkata: "Wahai Ibnu Abi Maryam, dalam shalat juga? Awas, awas!
45.en: As for the story's embellishment that ar-Rashid was addicted to wine and that his drunkenness coincided with that of his boon companions, Allah forbid! We know of no evil on his part. How can this be reconciled with ar-Rashid's state and his fulfilment of the duties of the caliphate in religion and justice, his association with scholars and saints, his conversations with al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, Ibn as-Sammak and al-'Umari, his correspondence with Sufyan ath-Thawri, his weeping at their admonitions, his prayer at Mecca during his circumambulation, his piety and his observance of the times of prayer, attending the dawn prayer at its earliest time? At-Tabari and others report that he used to pray a hundred supererogatory units every day, and to go on a raid one year and on pilgrimage the next. He once rebuked Ibn Abi Maryam, his jester in his evening entertainments, when he made such a joke during prayer: hearing ar-Rashid recite, 'Why should I not worship Him who created me?' (Qur'an 36:22), he said: 'By Allah, I do not know why!' Ar-Rashid could not help laughing, but then he turned to him angrily and said: 'O Ibn Abi Maryam, in prayer too? Beware, beware!
